The 43-23 process moves unique or original knowing into outward explanation; the new knowing must be structured and explained, and may otherwise be hard for others to understand.
The Channel of Talent 48-16 concerns perfected repetition of a pattern, illustrated by repeated rehearsal in pursuit of possible perfection.
Gate 18 challenges whether inherited or authoritative patterns are valid; the challenge may also confirm that a pattern is worthy rather than merely destroy it.
Gate 28 and the Channel of Struggle concern purposefulness and the question of whether struggle is worth it; the referenced fear is purposelessness, not literal physical death.

frozen_paraphrased_propositions.text: The page's gate descriptions explicitly apply when the activation is black or Personality-present and the gate is in a defined center; red or Design-only traits may not be consciously identified.
Gate 1 concerns unique self-expression in one's own way; Gate 8 concerns contribution and adding a new element for others.
Gate 5 concerns fixed rhythms, natural timing, habits, and resistance to interference with an established personal tempo.
Gate 16 concerns skill, enthusiasm, identification, and repeated practice toward high performance; Gate 48 concerns depth and functional solutions.
Gate 18 notices patterns that could be corrected and can challenge ineffective authority; Gate 58 supplies energy to improve and perfect things.
Gate 43 concerns unique insight and internally structured knowing; Gate 23 concerns assimilating resistance and explaining a new insight so it can be considered by others.
Gate 24 repeatedly ponders unique inspiration into rational form; Gate 61 supplies pressure to investigate mystery and deeper individual truth.
Gate 28 assesses whether risk and struggle make life worthwhile; Gate 38 supplies energy to oppose what obstructs a purposeful struggle.
Gate 30 concerns longing for new experience; Gate 32 concerns continuity, assessing potential, and instinct for business or financial management.

Gate 33 concerns privacy and reflective decompression after experience; Gate 35 seeks change and new experiences and may later share stories; Gate 36 concerns emotional crisis and desire for unfamiliar experience.
Gate 40 weighs work as a bargain against rest, autonomy, and relief from demands; Gate 41 supplies imaginative hunger and pressure toward new experience.
Gate 51 concerns competition, being first, and winning; Gate 54 concerns material ambition and advancement through hierarchy.
Gate 56 concerns stimulating others by turning reflected experience and ideas into narrative stories.
